name: Dethavar
description: Dethavar is a deep dissociative that selectively suppresses proprioceptive and interoceptive signaling while maintaining cognitive clarity, producing a state in which users experience consciousness as floating, unmoored from physical sensation — including from the persistent sensory noise of cybernetic augmentation. It is the drug of choice for heavily augmented individuals who find the constant mechanical feedback of their chrome psychologically exhausting or alienating. Nightshade developed it ostensibly as a 'chrome adaptation aid.'
effects: profound relief for those who experience body dysmorphia related to augmentation
side_effects: inability to operate chrome or physical systems during effect
disorientation upon return to body sensation
dangerous if augmentation requires active monitoring (cardiac chrome, respiratory assists)
chronic use causes permanent proprioceptive degradation — users lose sense of body even unmedicated
psychological dependency driven by desire to escape body
risk of accidental physical harm during floated state
cultural_context: Dethavar speaks to a specifically 2200 kind of suffering: the alienation of living in a body that's more machine than flesh, that hums and clicks and reports data streams instead of feelings. Heavily chromed Shelf workers — port loaders, factory operators, combat veterans — use Ghost to get a few hours of simply being a mind without a body. Tier 2 chrome addicts use it to escape the consequences of over-augmentation. It is almost never used by the unaugmented, who find the dissociation horrifying rather than relieving.
story_hooks: A port worker with 70% chrome coverage has been using Dethavar daily for a year; his proprioceptive degradation has reached the point where without the drug he feels like a stranger in his own chassis — and the drug no longer fully works
A Nightshade researcher embedded in the Shelf is documenting Dethavar use patterns — and quietly advocating internally that the company increase its addictive profile to expand the market

A heavily augmented corporate enforcer uses Ghost recreationally but took it before a job she didn't know was on the schedule — she's physically capable but completely disconnected from her body, and she has to complete the contract anyway
